A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Duoduo CLIP work and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends after the references; v2 includes Appendix A, which is included in this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, text-to-shape retrieval and model-ablation results in Section 4, Tables 2–6 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ScanObjectNN, ScanNet and further ablation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same CLIP-initialized multi-view encoder, contrastive objective, cross-view attention, embedding averaging and selective attention-layer training. v2 explicitly describes frozen MLPs and pose-free, permutation-invariant inputs, but these do not establish a changed procedure. MLP fine-tuning is introduced as an ablation.

E1.justification: v2 retains Objaverse-LVIS, MVImgNet/MVPNet and Text2Shape coverage and adds two distinct real-world evaluation settings: ScanObjectNN using rendered point-cloud views and ScanNet using cropped RGB video frames (Section 4.1 and Appendix A.3). These substantially broaden evaluation beyond the original data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding Objaverse-LVIS, MVPNet and Text2Shape comparisons. The added benchmarks reuse existing comparison methods, including OpenShape, TAMM, Uni3D and zero-shot CLIP. The new fine-tuning configurations are model ablations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces ScanObjectNN point-cloud rendering and ScanNet mask-ranked frame selection/cropping protocols. Appendix A adds camera-elevation controls, training-view ranges and MLP-tuning configurations, including a 1400 batch-size exception. These expand experimental settings substantially; the default 80-epoch, batch-1600 training remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention-map case studies (Figure 3), expands MVA testing across trainable-layer counts and three datasets (Table 6), and adds inference-cost, camera-sampling, training-view-count and MLP-freezing analyses (Appendices A.1–A.2). The original layer-count ablation is retained, while the Objaverse-LVIS six-inference-view MVA comparison is no longer reported.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluations are averaged over three seeds (v1 Section 4.2; v2 Section 4.2.1). v2 introduces no additional repeated-run policy, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Original Objaverse-LVIS and Text2Shape scores are retained. OpenShape† MVPNet Top1 changes from 3.55 to 10.80, and its MVPNet-trained counterpart from 54.35 to 54.59, alongside newly stated alignment preprocessing. New results include ScanObjectNN Top1 of 66.3 and ScanNet averages of 61.3/63.3 for trained variants versus 69.2 for zero-shot CLIP, plus extensive new ablation measurements.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the written attention expression: v1 places multiplication by V inside softmax, whereas v2 places it outside. This changes the mathematical expression rather than merely its notation. No new theorem or proof accompanies the newly emphasized permutation-invariance property.

C1.justification: v2 newly highlights permutation invariance and pose-free operation in the abstract. Its conclusion qualifies superiority relative to point-cloud methods trained similarly, replacing v1's claim about almost all quantitative metrics. The central efficiency, flexible-view representation and text-alignment contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends v1's geometry and synthetic-data-overfitting discussion. It connects frozen MLPs and fewer trained layers to preserved transfer, interprets attention maps as cross-view correspondence, and explains camera-coverage tradeoffs. ScanNet results motivate stronger data/overfitting limitations, while the conclusion adds alternative-pretraining and hybrid image/point-cloud directions.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds numerical camera ranges, timing and memory measurement settings, the batch-size exception, and concrete ScanObjectNN/ScanNet image-preparation instructions. v2 also newly states MVPNet up-axis alignment, without establishing whether that preprocessing changed from v1. The front-page resource link changes from a repository address to a project-page address.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for ScanNet, SceneNN, ScanObjectNN, CyCLIP and sigmoid-loss pretraining. It removes MiniGPT-3D alongside the associated LLM future-work discussion. The main related-work coverage and positioning against point-cloud and multi-view representation methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory and related-work prose, groups classification experiments and model ablations under Section 4.2, and rewrites 'Limitations and Future Work' as a fuller conclusion. Most existing method and results prose remains recognizable; the new scientific appendix does not by itself constitute extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds attention visualizations, camera-sampling illustrations and ScanObjectNN renders, plus Tables 7–12. Table 2 gains ScanObjectNN columns, and the MVA table is redesigned around layers and datasets. Schematics, typography and table placement also change, while original retrieval figures and view-count plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the training design and transfer claims through additional real-world benchmarks and targeted camera, view-count and MLP ablations. The appendix improves reproducibility and exposes limitations, particularly trained models trailing zero-shot CLIP on ScanNet. These gains outweigh limited reporting weaknesses, including claiming ScanObjectNN Top3 superiority where Table 2 shows a tie with Uni3D.
